headline: CMI Limited enters Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process
sum: CMI Limited, an industrial cables manufacturer, has been admitted into the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, as formally notified to the NSE.
implication: The admission triggers statutory moratorium under IBC s.14, freezing all creditor actions; the resolution professional assumes control of operations and must complete CIRP within 180 days (extendable by 90 days) to present a resolution plan for creditor voting.
detail: CMI Limited's entry into CIRP follows a default event and creditor petition filed before the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT). Upon admission, all existing management authority is suspended and vested in the insolvency resolution professional (IRP/RP). The company is now in the statutory 180-day window to solicit resolution plans from eligible bidders, which must be voted on by the committee of creditors (CoC). The CIRP process is designed to rehabilitate the company as a going concern or facilitate an orderly sale of assets.

framework.note: Automatic moratorium on all civil proceedings, debt recovery, and enforcement actions upon CIRP admission; central to IBC mechanics.
Functions and duties of the insolvency resolution professional; central to operational control.
CIRP completion timeline: 180 days from admission, extendable by up to 90 days by the NCLT; central deadline.
Resolution plan approval process and committee of creditors voting; central to exit mechanics.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy (Application to Individuals and Partnership Firms) Regulations, 2016; Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (Insolvency Resolution Process for Corporate Persons) Regulations, 2016
framework.note: Procedural rules for CIRP conduct, creditor meetings, RP appointment, and plan submission.
Jurisdiction and procedural framework for NCLT admission and supervision of CIRP.
Definition of corporate debtor; CMI Limited is subject to CA 2013 corporate governance post-emergence.

conditions: Moratorium under IBC s.14 in effect
Insolvency resolution professional appointed and taken charge
Committee of creditors constituted (creditors with >₹1 crore claim or top 100 creditors)
approvals: NCLT admission order (National Company Law Tribunal)
structure.novel: Standard CIRP admission under IBC; no novel structuring elements disclosed at filing stage.

triggers.note: Creditor or debtor petition triggering admission; IBC is the sole governing statute for corporate insolvency in India.
Mandatory disclosure to stock exchanges (NSE/BSE) of material corporate action, including CIRP admission.
Jurisdiction and appellate framework for CIRP oversight.
